input.quote: ARTICLE IV TERM I Subject to termination pursuant to this Agreement, the Non Exclusive license granted by Licensor to Licensee shall be for an initial period of 36 months, commencing from the acceptance date, (the "Initial Period").
input.rationale: Article IV fixes a 36-month Initial Period and gives Licensee no right to terminate for convenience anywhere in the Agreement; the only termination rights are Licensor's rights for Licensee breach, insolvency (Art. XIX, mutual), Change of Control (Art. XX) and Licensee wind-up (Art. XX(b)). Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is walk-away territory and fails the fallback, so we add a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. Licensor holds no convenience right, so no deletion is needed on that side.

ops.text: IV Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor, without penalty or early-termination charge. In such event, Licensor shall refund to Licensee any prepaid fees relating to the period after the effective date of termination, and Licensee shall have no obligation to make any payment in respect of any period after such date.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The 36-month Initial Period gives us no exit right, so we have added a Licensee termination for convenience on thirty (30) days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, consistent with our playbook position. If helpful we can move to 60 days' notice.
proposal.summary: Add Licensee termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees
